The test image shows a sugarcane leaf with a pale/whitish horizontal streak or stripe running along the midrib area. The leaf is mostly green with this distinct lighter band. - Sugarcane leaf (elongated, grass-like blade)
- A single, distinct pale/whitish stripe running lengthwise along the midrib/center vein
- The rest of the leaf tissue appears normal green
- No discrete spots, lesions, or mosaic patterning visible
- The stripe is bright, clean, and centered

**Reasoning:**
The single prominent pale/white stripe centered along the midrib of an otherwise green sugarcane leaf is the hallmark symptom of **Yellow_Leaf** syndrome (sugarcane yellow leaf virus), where the midrib undergoes chlorosis/yellowing, turning pale yellow to white. This is distinct from:
- Mosaic virus (which shows irregular mosaic green/yellow patches, not a single midrib stripe)
- Streak Mosaic (multiple narrow parallel streaks)
- Brown Spot / Yellow Spot (discrete circular/oval spots)
- Leaf Scald (white stripe along leaf margins, scalded appearance)
- Grassy Shoot (abnormal tillering, narrow leaves)

The clean single central stripe pattern most closely matches Yellow_Leaf midrib chlorosis.
